sources.title: OpenStreetMap RAD Building host footprint
sources.note: ODbL. The existing footprint on the northwest corner of Panganiban Drive and Blumentritt Street hosts selection and display for the surviving arch, which stands on its northeast edge along Blumentritt; it is not the historic mansion. Geometry is retained and edit dates are not construction dates. No construction date is assigned to the modern host. Corrected October 8, 2026 from way/23665222, the older building across Panganiban Drive.

sources.title: Naga City Ordinance No. 2003-003, Section 6
sources.note: Enacted January 15, 2003. Lists the Spanish-style gate ruins at Blumentritt Street corner Panganiban Avenue for preservation.

sources.title: Naga City Tourism: The Old Abella Mansion Arch
sources.note: Supports the arch, former mansion, Mariano Abella and the June 12, 2024 marker installation. Inspected October 8, 2026; its location is Abella Residence Arch, J5FQ+738, Panganiban Drive. Historical facts concern the arch or former mansion, not the RAD Building.

sources.title: Bicol Mail: Naga fetes Phil-Spanish Friendship Day
sources.note: July 4, 2019 report and JRM-PIA5 photograph inspected October 8, 2026. Identifies the arch within the RAD Building perimeter at Panganiban Drive and Blumentritt Street; the photograph shows the brick arch incorporated into the modern glass-fronted host. It reports an earlier June 30, 2019 marker unveiling; the 2024 installation is not claimed to be the first marker.

sources.title: Google Street View: arch at Panganiban and Blumentritt
sources.note: October 2025 panorama inspected October 8, 2026. The two red-brick gate piers, overgrown with bougainvillea, stand on the west side of Blumentritt Street just north of Panganiban Drive, in front of the modern glass-fronted building on the northwest corner. Google satellite at z21 places the same bougainvillea crown on the northeast edge of way/23671432. Capture dates are not construction dates; no image is saved or distributed.

text.en: The red-brick arch is the surviving remnant of Don Mariano Abella's former mansion.
Mariano Abella took part in the Propaganda Movement and served as provincial governor early in the American period.
Japanese forces occupied the former mansion during World War II.
Naga City Tourism records a historical marker installation at the site on June 12, 2024.
